conditions: Re-run AERMOD with a full year of urban met data
Calibrate the MIKE 21 plume model to field TSS
Add SSP2-4.5 / SSP5-8.5 sea-level and storm-surge checks
Cost the EMP and add stop-work triggers

findings.title: Category B despite 15 million m³ of dredging
findings.quote: the proposed WCT-1 terminal Project has been assessed as 'Category B' Project
findings.fix: Re-screen as Category A (large capital dredging and reclamation in a marine setting) or justify Category B against lender criteria.

findings.title: Site and layout fixed in the 2005 EIA; no alternatives or no-project option
findings.quote: The EIA Report 2005, as an option assessment exercise initially considered nine layout options, of which two were shortlisted
findings.fix: Add an alternatives chapter: borrow-site options, dredging methods, phasing and a no-project baseline.

findings.title: Stakeholder chapter aims to combat stakeholder influence
findings.quote: taking appropriate measures to combat their influence
findings.fix: Reframe engagement around disclosure and response (IFC PS1 / WB ESS10), with a grievance log.

findings.title: Four-day site visit; baseline lab hired by proponent
findings.quote: The ESIA report has been prepared based on the site assessment undertaken in 9-12 November 2022
findings.fix: Extend baseline to cover both monsoons and use an independent accredited lab.

findings.title: AERMOD met input is one season; text says WRF 2022; dispersion Rural
findings.quote: One season meteorological data (from 01 April 2019 to 30 June 2019)
findings.fix: Re-run AERMOD with a full year of site met data and urban dispersion coefficients.

findings.title: 24-hour baseline vs 1-hour standards; PM10 120 vs 100 µg/m³ at AQ3
findings.fix: Compare 1-hour maxima with 1-hour standards; treat AQ3 as already exceeding for PM10.

findings.title: MIKE 21 plume: assumed ambient SSC, no calibration, cycle 425 vs 415 min
findings.quote: The total duration of each dredging cycle is 415 min (approximately 7 hrs)
findings.fix: Calibrate the plume model against the March 2023 TSS survey and reconcile the cycle time.

findings.title: Plume "may extend to 4 km"; effect "minimal" beyond dredging zone
findings.quote: sediment plume may extend to 4 km from the borrow area
findings.fix: State the predicted TSS concentration at named receptors and distances, with a threshold to test against.

findings.title: Tsunami assessment left as a placeholder
findings.quote: Advisian team to provide their assessment regarding the same before any finalization
findings.fix: Complete the tsunami assessment before the ESIA is accepted as final.

findings.title: Storm surge rated Remote from history only; no sea-level rise
findings.quote: Likelihood Remote The site has not faced any storm surge related risk
findings.fix: Assess surge and overtopping under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 to 2075.

findings.title: GHG 21,473 tCO₂ (2031–32) is 86% of the 25,000 t threshold, rising
findings.fix: Add a GHG management plan and annual reporting trigger before the 25,000 t threshold.

findings.title: EMP budget has no figure (USD 650 M project)
findings.quote: The Contractors and CWIT will allocate a separate budget
findings.fix: Give the EMP a line-item budget with responsible party and timing.

findings.title: 23 EMP items say "Training: None"; "should" used throughout
findings.quote: Training: None Resource: EPC Contractors will be responsible for EMP implementation
findings.fix: Replace hedges with firm commitments and add training for dredging, spill and waste items.

findings.title: Monitoring lacks reef/benthos, beach profile, underwater noise, GHG
findings.fix: Add benthic, shoreline, underwater-noise and GHG monitoring rows with frequency and thresholds.

findings.title: TSS 114–148 mg/l vs MEPA 150; 12 of 28 ≥ 140
findings.quote: The suspended solids level ranged from 114 to 146 m/l, which is within the MEPA limit of 150 mg/l
findings.fix: Treat the borrow area as near-saturated; set a stop-work trigger at 150 mg/l 500 m from the dredger.

findings.title: IFC climate-resilience guideline marked Applicable but not assessed
findings.quote: Climate change resilience Port and terminal facilities are vulnerable to the direct and indirect impacts of climate change
findings.fix: Assess projected climate impacts in design, as the IFC Ports guideline requires.
